# Structural modelling and analysis-method sources

Checked **17 Sep 2026**. These public primary-source pages were retrieved.
Summaries are original; no source figures, standard tables or course notes are
bundled. The check date does not establish adoption of a building-code edition.

## S1 — MIT OpenCourseWare: Mechanics & Materials I, lecture notes

- URL: https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/2-001-mechanics-materials-i-fall-2006/pages/lecture-notes/
- Checked: 17 Sep 2026; official course-page HTML retrieved.
- Relevance: the course organizes statics around forces, moments and equilibrium,
  then treats truss response, shear/bending diagrams, force-deformation relations,
  indeterminacy and beam deflection. This informs the separation of drawn member
  geometry from a declared mechanical problem and the selection of independently
  specified analytical regression cases.
- Applicability limits: undergraduate mechanics teaching, not a building code,
  design approval or ready-made HomePlanner solver. The lecture index and topic
  descriptions were reviewed; no downloaded lecture solution was claimed as an
  executed benchmark. Any future fixture must state its own loading, restraints,
  units, material/constitutive assumptions and expected solution.

## S2 — NASA: NASA-STD-7009, models and simulations

- URL: https://standards.nasa.gov/standard/NASA/NASA-STD-7009
- Checked: 17 Sep 2026; official standard landing-page content retrieved.
- Relevance: the page describes modelling/simulation practices across development
  and use, credibility assessment, and project-defined acceptance criteria; it
  identifies NASA-STD-7009B and the need for discipline-specific practices.
  This supports recording intended use, evidence, uncertainty and validation
  criteria separately from a model's presentation or provenance label.
- Applicability limits: NASA programme governance is not residential structural
  design regulation or a local engineer's approval. The landing-page scope was
  reviewed, not every normative clause. No NASA compliance, verification level
  or certification is claimed for HomePlanner.

## Access and authority boundaries

Neither source supplies project loads, material strengths, geotechnical data,
adopted building-code combinations or safe member dimensions. No paywalled
structural standard was reproduced or assumed to have been reviewed.
Current jurisdiction, code edition/amendments and professional responsibility
remain unresolved until supplied for the particular project.

Use source applicability before numerical thresholds. Software geometry tolerances,
academic analytical cases and a successful equilibrium check are not physical
construction tolerances, comprehensive design checks or permission to demolish.
Public research must never contain private code, coordinates, plans or user records.
